### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/knowledge-memory`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **44** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9171bed0a65ab242567f243969368ead786cd830`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 42 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9171bed0a65ab242567f243969368ead786cd830` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `99f48902f4d11cae1fef938986d85c78bb8309b2` — the merge of head `6e978db363c73dc9d151549ef46d6c141bc679ac` into base `9171bed0a65ab242567f243969368ead786cd830`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 99f48902f4d11cae1fef938986d85c78bb8309b2 && git checkout 99f48902f4d11cae1fef938986d85c78bb8309b2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9171bed0a65ab242567f243969368ead786cd830 6e978db363c73dc9d151549ef46d6c141bc679ac && git checkout -B drift-repro 9171bed0a65ab242567f243969368ead786cd830 && git merge --no-ff 6e978db363c73dc9d151549ef46d6c141bc679ac

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9171bed0a65ab242567f243969368ead786cd830
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9171bed0a65ab242567f243969368ead786cd830` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3df745d2a1328770687e0f93ecc5e7b5f29ca946`
Local-runs: probe — the zone's ablation counts and the plugin-wiring pin could only be measured by running the two vitest suites at this head, in a throwaway worktree that is now removed
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-document.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-adapter.ts + packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-organization-scope.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-source-admission.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/testing.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/index.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json, content/docs/references/ai/knowledge-document.mdx, content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx

### ① Derived judgments

- PR #37256 (draft) for card #37097, epic #37000, ADR-0161 K8 item 9. Owed tier by `record-recognisers --template --paths`: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, schema face, hits = the two spec files.
- K = 0 (merge-base is origin/main `d62f9e9c05a4`); `git merge-tree` against origin/main is clean (tree `488f14a6030c`); GitHub reads `mergeable_state: clean`.
- Check-runs at this head, read 2026-11-25T08:31Z: 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 running. The skipped ones are opt-in or queue-only jobs (Lint UI, UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, one Dogfood matrix placeholder, packed-tarball smoke, the two queue verdicts, the schedule gate, the 18.x upgrade harness).
- Local at this head: knowledge-memory 29/29, service-knowledge 192/192; `pnpm check:system-context-census` OK (202 sites, register matches).
- Ablations re-run here, each restored: memory filter off → 6 red; organization left out of the hash → 2 red (1 contract, 1 service); service hands no `organizationIds` → 4 + 5 red. All three match the report.
- Further ablations of mine, each red by at least one case: `[]` read as "no filter" in the adapter (1); a document with no organization ranked by a filtered search (4); a `deny` verdict returned as `undefined` (3); the search failing open on an unreadable posture (1); the event sync assembling without the posture (1); `isolated` answered with the membership set (1).
- One ablation stayed green: see S1.
- Overlap: of 42 other open PRs only #35129 touches these packages, and only their `CHANGELOG.md` / `package.json`, which this diff does not touch.

### ② Semver level

- `Metadata-protocol: added` holds. `KnowledgeDocument.organizationId` and `AdapterSearchOptions.organizationIds` are both optional; nothing is removed, renamed or tightened; the schema is a plain `z.object`, so a document without the key parses as before. Both are K8 item 9's members and land with their first reader and suite cases (K8 rules 1 and 2).
- spec `minor`, service-knowledge and knowledge-memory `patch`: the same levels as #37096's changeset for the same kind of change.
- `implements.organizationIds` is a new required key of the contract suite's options. That is not a break for a published consumer: the suite arrived with #37096, whose changeset is still unreleased (service-knowledge is at 18.6.0 with no CHANGELOG entry for it).
- `recordToDocument` gains an optional fifth argument and `computeDocHash` an optional member of its `Pick`; existing calls compile and hash as before (pinned byte-for-byte against the old recipe).
- `Clause-②: yes` holds: a published schema and a contract interface change.
- `Skills-docs: none` holds: `skills/**` names `IKnowledgeAdapter` once, in `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, as the thing a `KnowledgeSource` points at; no skill teaches the document shape, the search options, the hash or the suite.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation "regenerated artifacts": accepted, both are generator output and `check:generated` is green in CI.
- Deviation "`knowledge-service-plugin.ts`": verified, +20 lines, one import and one constructor option; the mount path and the embedder logic are not in the diff.
- Deviation "no `scripts/adr-anchors` entry": accepted, outside the file surface (N4).
- Deviation "16 of 117 gates re-run after the last two commits": accepted, CI ran the whole set at this head and is green.
- Out-of-scope note on `system-context.mdx` row 46: agreed, no new row is owed (N1).
- Open question (docHash recipe): answered below, option A, with M1.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no new in-app join or id materialisation where SQL could do it. The service hands the adapter the organization set, so a SQL adapter (#37100) filters in its own `WHERE`; `knowledge-memory` is an in-process store and filters its own array.

### ④ Design judgment

Claims checked against the code at this head:

1. Server-side computation holds. `searchOrganizationIds` feeds `computeTenantLayer0Verdict` from `ctx.tenantId` / `ctx.accessible_org_ids` and the posture from `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture`; it maps the verdict and derives nothing. The object facts come from `engine.getSchema`, the same source `plugin-security` prefers for the wall's own field set. `isPlatformAdmin` and `posturePermitsCrossTenant` are passed `false`, which can only narrow.
2. `[]` versus `undefined` holds, and I found no path where a caller behind a wall gets `undefined` that the wall itself would not also answer `none`. The exits that hand no filter are: the system identity; a `file` / `http` source; the `single` posture or no `tenancy` service; an object with tenancy disabled or with no `organization_id` column. No context or no engine drops every `object` source before the scope is asked. An unreadable posture drops them too. An unreadable schema reads as a walled object. `deny` maps to `[]`.
3. Input rejection holds: `KnowledgeSearchOptions` has no organization member, the adapter options are built fresh, a caller's `filter.organizationIds` stays inside `filter` (pinned), `search_knowledge` refuses the argument (pinned), `indexDocument` throws before the upsert (pinned).
4. `knowledge-memory` filters the chunk list before the metadata filter and before scoring; `applyPermissionFilter` is not in the diff.
5. The move in `44494ec2` is behaviour-preserving for every caller that is not the system identity: before it, `scopeByOrganization` skipped on `!ctx || ctx.isSystem`; after it, the system identity returns earlier and the no-context branch has already dropped the `object` sources. Every other caller still reaches `scopeByOrganization`.

Findings:

- M1 (must-fix) — the hash recipe of K8 item 2 changes here without the dated note that K8 rule 3 names as the form of such a change. The note on ADR-0161 (items 2 and 9) lands first; this PR then proceeds unchanged on that point. Reason for the order: this PR lands on a review record, while `docs/adr` is the maintainer's to approve, so merging first would settle his decision for him, and a recipe that has shipped is costly to flip (each flip rewrites documents).
- S1 (should-fix) — the plugin's `resolveTenancyPosture` wiring has no pin. Replacing it with `async () => undefined` in `knowledge-service-plugin.ts` leaves both suites green (29/29, 192/192). It is the only production reader of the posture; if it breaks, every deployment reads as `single`: no document is stamped and no filter is handed, silently. One plugin-level case over a kernel with a `tenancy` service (walled → the adapter is handed the set; none registered → no filter; registered and throwing → no `object` source searched) closes it.
- S2 (should-fix) — the contract text does not say that an adapter storing `docHash` has to store `organizationId` from the same version on. K8 rule 2 lets an adapter take up item 2 before item 9. Such an adapter stores a hash that already covers the organization while holding no organization; when it later starts to read item 9, a complete reindex skips every document (the hashes match) and a walled search never ranks them. It fails toward ranking nothing, and it is the same under option B. One sentence on `KnowledgeDocument.organizationId` in the spec TSDoc, repeated in the dated note, is enough.
- N1 — `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 46 needs no new row: the bypass is the same `admitSources` read, no elevation site was added, and the census is green. Its prose could add that the system identity is also handed no organization scope; that is the page owner's call.
- N2 — under `single` the function returns before the verdict is asked, so the `outsideEveryOrganization` input is never read (the walled rungs ignore it). A person outside every organization is therefore handed no filter where the verdict says `deny`; the re-read still returns nothing. Either let the verdict answer under `single` too, or drop the input.
- N3 — the plugin types the `tenancy` service inline rather than as core's `TenancyPostureSource`, and its sync leg repeats the not-registered handling `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` already does.
- N4 — no `scripts/adr-anchors` entry for K8 item 9; a follow-up outside this file surface.
- N5 — an event sync whose posture read throws is logged at `warn` and leaves the stored document as it was; no case pins that path.
- N6 — for #37099: a build that runs at boot before the `tenancy` service is registered reads "no wall" and stamps nothing. The next complete reindex repairs it (the hash differs), but the card should read the posture after the kernel is ready.

**The docHash question: option A, and the ADR note lands before this PR.**
Correctness. Under A the hash covers the organization whenever the document has one, so every change that should rewrite a document changes its hash: a document gaining an organization (the upgrade, or a deployment moving from `single` to a walled posture), losing one, or moving from one organization to another with no content change. A complete reindex therefore never leaves a stale stamp, with the one adapter-side exception S2 names, which B shares. Under B the first reindex after the version bump is correct, but nothing after it is: a record that moves organization, or a deployment that turns its wall on later, keeps its hash, the reindex skips it, and the stamp stays wrong until an event happens to touch that record. Reconcile exists because events are missed (K1), so B leaves a hole the reindex was built to close: the old organization keeps a ranking place the re-read empties, and the new one never sees the document ranked.
Contract fidelity. Item 2 decides "a hash of the assembled document"; the three parts in its parenthesis were the whole assembled document when it was accepted. Item 9 then makes the organization part of what the service sets at assembly. A keeps item 2's meaning and outdates its parenthesis; B keeps the parenthesis and gives up the meaning. The recipe is also not something an adapter reads: it stores the hash as given. So A is an amendment to the record, not a departure from the contract, and K8 rule 3 gives the form: a dated note.
Which is harder for AI-written code to get wrong. A keeps one rule, "the hash covers what the service assembled", and the suite holds it from both sides (the byte-for-byte pin of the old recipe, and the upgrade case). B adds a second rule a later author has to remember, "organization changes reach the index by events only", with nothing in the reindex path to fail when it is forgotten. A's one trap is the conditional inclusion: a later optional member has to enter the hash the same way (absent means omitted), or the version has to be bumped; the note should say so.
Order. Before. The note is the maintainer's decision on a governed path, and this PR would otherwise land without him and fix the recipe in shipped indexes. K = 0 and nothing else open touches these files, so waiting costs little.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6e978db363c73dc9d151549ef46d6c141bc679ac`
Local-runs: probe — the new plugin describe and its ablation count could only be measured by running the service-knowledge suite at this head, in a throwaway worktree that is now removed
Scope: delta `3df745d2a132..6e978db363c7` (two commits) — packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-document.zod.ts + packages/services/service-knowledge/src/__tests__/knowledge-service.test.ts, read against packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service-plugin.ts, knowledge-service.ts and knowledge-organization-scope.ts (unchanged since record 7157191417)

Delta record. It continues the record at `3df745d2a132` (comment 7157191417); what that record verified and this one does not restate still stands, because no production file changed.

### ① Derived judgments

- The delta is two commits. `e8b0688fe86c` adds 93 lines to `knowledge-service.test.ts` and 4 TSDoc lines to `knowledge-document.zod.ts`. `6e978db363c7` rewrites those TSDoc lines only (+3/−4, one file, inside one comment block). No `.describe()` text, no schema member, no production source and no generated artifact is in either commit; the PR's file list is the same 15 files.
- All local runs below were made at `6e978db363c7` itself, so nothing rests on the earlier head. Had they been made at `e8b0688fe86c` they would carry over unchanged: the diff between the two heads is comment text.
- Local at this head: service-knowledge 197/197 (192 + 5 new), knowledge-memory 29/29, `pnpm check:system-context-census` OK (202 sites, register matches).
- The zone's ablation reproduces: the plugin's `resolveTenancyPosture` set to `async () => undefined` gives 3 red (both walled cases and the unreadable case) and leaves the no-tenancy case green, 194/197. Restored.
- Probes of mine, each restored. Running the no-tenancy and the unreadable case on `ObjectKernel` instead of `LiteKernel`: both green, so the production kernel answers the two the same way. Removing the `getServiceAsync` leg from the wiring: 197/197 green (N7). Making the sync leg swallow every throw: 197/197 green (N7).
- K = 5 against origin/main `ede9b91f402b` (merge-base still `d62f9e9c05a4`); `git merge-tree` is clean (tree `784154079e9e`); none of the five commits touches a knowledge package, the two spec files or core's security or kernel code. GitHub reads `mergeable_state: unknown` on a draft.
- Check-runs at this head, read 2026-11-25T09:35Z: 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 running. The skipped ten are the same opt-in and queue-only jobs as at the prior head.
- The two `failure` rows at `e8b0688fe86c` (`Test UI`, `TypeScript Type Check`) are a cancel cascade and not a test result: they are the two aggregate jobs, they ran four seconds each at 2026-11-25T09:03:50Z, right after their shards were cancelled at 2026-11-25T09:03:46Z by the push of `6e978db363c7` (2026-11-25T09:00:32Z). 27 runs there are `cancelled`; no shard reads `failure`.
- ADR note PR #37263 (docs-only, draft, head `dd1756af23aa`) is open and not merged, read 2026-11-25T09:35Z.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged from the prior record. The delta adds no member, changes no accept-set and no signature. `organizationId` keeps its `.describe()` text, so the generated reference page and `authorable-surface/ai.json` are untouched, and the changeset needs no edit.
- `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Clause-②: yes` and `Skills-docs: none` hold as before.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- `skipSystemValidation: true` in the harness is a test-only setting. In `ObjectKernel` it gates two things, the pre-injection of in-memory fallbacks for core services and the missing-service validation; neither is on the path under test (`tenancy` is not a core-requirement service, and the plugin resolves it through `ctx.getKernel().getServiceAsync`). It masks no production path: the wiring that runs is the plugin's own, and my probe shows the same answers with the flag on for the no-tenancy and unreadable cases. The only other user in the tree is a plugin-auth test fixture.
- The cases reach the production wiring. `KnowledgeServicePlugin` is constructed and booted by a real kernel; the service under test is the one the plugin registered, fetched from the kernel; only the adapter and the `objectql` and `tenancy` services are stand-ins. The ablation above is the proof: a mutation in `knowledge-service-plugin.ts` turns the cases red.
- SQL push-down: nothing in the delta reads data.
- Not done by the zone and accepted as carried: N2, N3, N4. Main was not merged; K = 5 with a clean merge-tree, so nothing is owed for that before the landing sync.

### ④ Design judgment

Prior items, by id:

- S1 — closed. The describe "KnowledgeServicePlugin reads the tenancy posture from the kernel" drives the real plugin on `LiteKernel` and `ObjectKernel`: walled → the adapter is handed `['org_a']`; no `tenancy` service → no `organizationIds` key; registered and throwing → `[]` and `adapter.search` not called. The mutation the finding named (`async () => undefined`) now fails three cases.
- S2 — closed. The sentence at this head reads: "An adapter that stores `docHash` stores `organizationId` from the same version on; otherwise, once it starts reading this field, a complete reindex skips its documents and a walled search never ranks them." It is true to the code. `computeDocHash` includes `organizationId` whenever the document has one; the reindex skip compares the stored hash with the computed one and nothing else; so an adapter that kept the hash and dropped the organization has matching hashes, is skipped, and holds no organization for its own filter to match. It is also the wording of the note in #37263, so the two texts agree. The first version of the sentence (at `e8b0688fe86c`) said the same with the reason spelled out; the rewrite loses nothing a reader needs (N8).
- N5 — closed. The new case pins the path: the posture read throws inside `syncRecord`, the catch logs at `warn` with the reason, and neither `upsert` nor `delete` is called.
- N1, N2, N3, N4, N6 — carried unchanged; none is touched by the delta.

On N5's behaviour, warn and keep. It is safe as stated, with one consequence worth writing down. The row is re-read before the posture is read, so a row that is gone or no longer matches is still deleted from the index; only a row that still matches is kept as stored. That stored document can then be stale in content or in organization (the record was edited, or moved to another organization, while the posture was unreadable). A stale organization means the old organization's callers can still have the document take a ranking place; the permission re-read then returns nothing for them, so nothing is served across the wall, and the new organization does not see it ranked. The repair is the row's next event or a complete reindex (the hash differs). Both alternatives are worse: an upsert without the posture would write an unstamped document, and a delete would drop a document whose row still matches. A reindex under the same fault refuses to write, so the two paths agree. The gap is the same class as a missed event, which K1's reconcile exists for.

Findings:

- M1 (must-fix) — unchanged and still open: the hash recipe of K8 item 2 changes here, and the dated note that K8 rule 3 names as the form of such a change has not landed. The note is PR #37263, open and unmerged at the time of this record. Nothing in this PR's code is asked to change; the note lands first.
- N7 — the two kernel cases pin that the wiring works on each kernel, not which leg serves it.
